result.summary: Validated CODE-DESIGNER Step 01 artefacts for DDL-05, MIG-01, MIG-02, MIG-03 (stage 16). All 20 acceptance criteria across the four requirements traced to specific design sections. No implementation code leaked (Type E docs contain only Zig signatures/types, no bodies; no SQL DDL outside the Type C YAML). DDL-05 correctly scoped as a standalone namespace predicate independent of DDL-01/ValidatePlatformDDL machinery (explicit "Must NOT depend on any DDL-01 type that does not yet exist"), verified it defines its own minimal StatementDescriptor/Actor types so it compiles and is testable standalone. MIG-02/MIG-03 fanout design verified against actual current contents of src/db/pool.zig, src/db/provisioning.zig, src/db/migrations.zig: schemaNameForTenant is public (pool.zig:137), Pool.acquire/release exist (pool.zig:802/857), the SELECT storage_mode FROM public.tenant citation at "pool.zig:190" is exact, the SET LOCAL search_path TO {schema},public pattern matches the existing convention at migrations.zig:443, and the documented non-reuse of runForSchema/public.schema_migrations (wrong grain -- would reintroduce a two-trackers-disagreeing bug) is a correct, justified design choice, not an oversight. Migration number 1144 confirmed as next-free (1143 is current max). tools/lint_design_artefact.py: 0 BLOCKER / 0 MAJOR on all three artefacts (ddl-05 doc: clean; mig-02-mig-03 doc: 5 MINOR -- E030 flags on public.tenant/public.schema_migrations qualification that is deliberate and documented, same exception MIG-01 YAML already carries for platform.platform_migrations, plus one E060 regex false-positive on the word "explicitly"; mig-01 YAML: clean). tools/codegen_migration.py --dry-run on the MIG-01 YAML exits 0 and its preview (CREATE TABLE + 5 test cases) covers all 5 MIG-01 ACs. Two MINOR traceability gaps noted for CODE-DESIGNER awareness (non-blocking): MIG-02 AC5 ("no code path writes a tenant control row on a connection other than the one applying that tenant DDL") and MIG-03 AC3 (different migration_id values may run concurrently) are both correctly implemented in the design (visible in the applyToTenant diagram and the module-purpose prose respectively) but, unlike every other AC in the same document, are not explicitly tagged by AC number -- a one-line annotation gap, not a substance gap; BACKEND-DEV has no ambiguity to resolve from it.

issues.description: mig-02-mig-03-platform-migration-fanout.md: MIG-02 AC5 ("No code path writes a tenant's control row on a connection other than the one applying that tenant's DDL") is correctly implemented (visible in the applyToTenant flow diagram, lines ~186-216, and reinforced by the DdlStep transaction-ownership constraint in Dependencies) but is never explicitly cited by AC number the way MIG-02 AC1-AC4 are in the Error taxonomy table. Recommend adding an explicit "MIG-02 AC5" citation near the applyToTenant diagram or in the Error taxonomy table for consistency with the rest of the document. Non-blocking.

mig-02-mig-03-platform-migration-fanout.md: MIG-03 AC3 ("two different migration_id values may execute concurrently") is correctly implemented (module purpose bullet: "different migration IDs may run concurrently, since the lock key is derived from migration_id") but, unlike MIG-03 AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5, is never explicitly tagged "MIG-03 AC3" anywhere in the document. Recommend adding the explicit tag for consistency. Non-blocking.

lint_design_artefact.py reports 5 MINOR findings on mig-02-mig-03-platform-migration-fanout.md: 4x E030 (schema-qualified public.tenant / public.schema_migrations) and 1x E060 (regex false-positive matching the English word "explicitly" as a malformed requirement ID). Verified both are false positives / deliberate documented exceptions, not defects: the design explicitly justifies qualifying public.tenant and public.schema_migrations because platform is never in any tenant search_path (same exception MIG-01's YAML documents for platform.platform_migrations). No action needed; recorded for the record per lint tool output.
